title: "It just made me sluggish" — sluggish, the pill on the desk, the orange
text:
“It just made me sluggish and my thoughts were unclear,” says Sophie the next morning to the nurse who has once again brought her two cups - one with water and one with a pill.

“Well, at least you gave it a try” she says “If you decide to take the pill it’ll be right here.” She leaves it on the desk and after she leaves the room Sophie stares at it, then pushes the tissue box in front of it so it’s out of her line of vision. She leans her head back against her pillow, then takes the orange that is on her night table, presses one long fingernail into it’s pristine back, and begins to peel.

text: As she’s walking out the door she glances down into the water cup which is on top and notices the pill is sitting there listlessly, barely dissolved still sitting in flakes and chunks at the bottom of the cup. “There is steel moh peel Mees Sophie,” says the nurse as though Sophie would have no idea and Sophie’s smile wavers. The nurse walks back over to where she is standing and Sophie puts the cup to her mouth but doesn’t let any liquid drip down past the barrier of her teeth. The nurse takes the cup. “You must swallow the peel.” “I already took half. I don’t want the other half. It’s too big. It’s not the right size for me,” she says, hoping that perhaps the nurse might grasp the simple concept of ratio as its been presented in this context. “Eet eez ahp to you.” says the nurse and Sophie beams at her once again. “But if you do not take de whole theeng I will have to write that you refuse.” The nurse leaves the cup with the very small amount of water and the half disintegrated pill on her night table and repeats: “Eet eez ahp to you,” then leaves the room.

title: The soap — the window over New York, the bar of soap, the cup
text: Sophie stares repeatedly at the pill and then goes to the window and undoes the blinds so the city of New York unfolds before her, filtered through the shatter proof plastic of the windows. She holds the pill cup in her hand, goes to the bathroom and unwraps the new bar of soap she’s gotten delivered that day. She breaks off tiny pieces of it and, after flushing the contents of the cup down the toilet, drips a small amount of water into the cup and sprinkles the cracked pieces of soap in the bottom of the cup. Then she leaves the room holding the cup triumphantly out in front of her.

title: The half pill takes hold — crayon, butter, sugar, the push-up
videos: Nurse Edna — the Meds clip (the morning meds nurse)
text: As she sits in the dark she begins to feel strange as the half pill takes ahold of her. She opens her drawer and pulls out a blue crayon, using it to create thick strokes on a blank menu, repeating the action violently until the paper rips in multiple places. Then she opens her drawer once again and pulls out one of her beloved butter pats. She peels off the lid but instead of taking it to the bathroom to carefully wash, dry, and include in one of her sculptures, she smears it on the pictures she’s been working on and then all over the walls and floor near the entrance of her room. Where she has smeared the butter, she opens a packet of sugar and empties it everywhere the butter is smeared so the butter is being used as glue. She arranges herself in a push-up position on the floor, over a pile of butter and sugar and holds herself there, with her eyes shut tight, grimacing. She stays there for a long time as the clock ticks loudly on the wall.

title: The end of the hallway — take the pill / don't take the pill
text: She sits at the end of the hallway, next to the hallway which patients go in as they choose. It’s never been locked so long as she’s been there but there is no handle on the inside of the door. mulling over the matter of whether or not to take the pill she’s been prescribed. “Take the pill,” she mutters, clenching her fists tightly, then releasing, and the antithesis: “Don’t take the pill,” she clenches her fists again. She repeats these two phrases eleven times in a row before screwing up her eyes in concentration as though the decision were laid out in front of her and she has just to interpret it in order to know what to do. She gives up and resorts to clenching her fists again, muttering those words over and over so it sounds like a mantra.
